rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past form depicts a certain future as already past; alternatively, the clause is circumstantial with an implicit قد, so the tense needs no such reinterpretation.
rows.anchor: وجاء فعل { وقيل } بصيغة المضي وهو واقع في المستقبل لأنه لتحقق وقوعه نزل منزلة فعل مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taste is a metaphor for bodily sensation: the tongue's sense is stronger than the skin's, and the comparison rests on intensity.
rows.anchor: والذوق : مستعار لإحساس ظاهر الجسد لأن إحساس الذوق باللسان أشد من إحساس ظاهر الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tasted punishment repays their worldly acquisition of shirk and its practices; equating punishment with their deeds stresses just recompense corresponding to their actions.
rows.anchor: والمذوق : هو العذاب فهو جزاء ما اكتسبوه في الدنيا من الشرك وشرائعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording تكسبون instead of تعملون attributes the punishment to what they acquired, cutting off the protest of people who resent their torment.
rows.anchor: فجيء بالصلة الدالة على أن ما ذاقوه جزاء ما اكتسبوه قطعا لتبرمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account answers believers who wonder why deniers still enjoy worldly blessings and wish their punishment would come sooner.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني لأن ما ذكر قبله من مصير المشركين إلى سوء العذاب يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples were punished in this world without warning or expectation; worldly punishment is disgrace, while the afterlife punishment repays wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: إذ أتاهم العذاب في الدنيا بدون إنذار غير مترقبين مجيئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء makes denial the cause of punishment; since Arab polytheists also denied the Messenger, they faced the same warning of punishment.
rows.anchor: الفاء في قوله : { فأتاهم العذاب } دالة على تسبب التكذيب في إتيان العذاب إليهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur reports that Muqatil, described as a leading Murjiʾi, argued that faith wipes away the worst deeds; since the verse describes piety from shirk, he took the worst deeds to mean major sins committed after faith.
rows.anchor: أن مقاتلا كان شيخ المرجئة وهم الذين يقولون لا يضر شيء من المعاصي مع الإيمان واحتج بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur answers that أسوأ is open to contextual interpretation and other evidence opposes using the verse's generality to support the Murjiʾi inference.
rows.anchor: وجوابه : لأن الأسوأ محتمل أن أدلة كثيرة أخرى تعارض الاستدلال بعمومها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing أسوأ with أحسن creates antithesis (ṭibāq).
rows.anchor: وفي الجمع بين كلمة { أسوأ } وكملة { أحسن } محسن الطبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding parable of the one master and contentious partners provokes idolaters to defend their gods and threaten the Messenger, leading into this reassurance.
rows.anchor: لما ضرب الله مثلا للمشركين والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf and al-Qurṭubi report that Quraysh feared their gods would harm the Prophet because he insulted them.
rows.anchor: أن قريشا قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives an account similar to the report that Quraysh threatened the Prophet with harm from their idols.
rows.anchor: وفي ( تفسير ابن عطية ) ما هو بمعنى هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat resembles Abraham's people calling for him to be burned and urging support for their gods.
rows.anchor: كما قال مشركو قوم إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, whom the Prophet alone worships, suffices against the polytheists and their false gods; the opening reassurance also hastens their dismay and the Prophet's comfort.
rows.anchor: لظهور أن المقصود كافيك أذاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying order would put their threats first and God's protection after; the wording is rearranged for effect. Alternatively, the first sentence is independent and the threat clause circumstantial.
rows.anchor: وأصل النظم : ويخوفونك بالذين من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Prophet عبده instead of using direct address directs the statement to the polytheists; the omitted object of كاف is their harm, and the question rebukes their belief that idols can harm him without a protector.
rows.anchor: ووقع التعبير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالاسم الظاهر وهو { عبده } دون ضمير الخطاب لأن المقصود توجيه الكلام إلى المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant is certainly the Prophet by the following address; his designation as God's servant honors him and assures that God will not hand him over to enemies.
rows.anchor: والمراد ب { عبده } هو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لا محالة وبقرينة و { يخوفونك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person reference to direct address is iltifāt, focusing the threat sentence specifically on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في { ويخوفونك } للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو التفات من ضمير الغيبة العائد على { عبده }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those beside God are idols; the rational relative form is conventional for them, and the omitted relative clause means that the polytheists took or worshipped them apart from God.
rows.anchor: عبر عنهم وهم حجارة بموصول العقلاء

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī gives as a revelation occasion Khalid ibn al-Walid's mission against al-ʿUzzā: its keeper warned him, then Khalid broke the idol; threats to Khalid were meant for the Prophet, making the verse Medinan.
rows.anchor: تفسير البيضاوي ) أن سبب نزول هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says the Medinan occasion does not fit the context and suggests the story may only illustrate a familiar idol threat.
rows.anchor: ولعل بعض من قال هذا إنما أراد الاستشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers have the singular عبده; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Abū Jaʿfar, and Khalaf read plural عباده, referring to the Prophet and believers whom God protects.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { بكاف عبده }

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intervening statement portrays their misguidance as deeply rooted in their nature and generations, so attributing its creation to God implies it is exceptionally hard to uproot.
rows.anchor: قصد من هذا الاعتراض أن ضلالهم داء عياء لأنه ضلال مكون في نفوسهم وجبلتهم قد ثبتته الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying that they have a guide is a figurative way to deny that they attain guidance; Ibn Ashur links the formulation to al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: وأريد من نفي الهادي من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both this wording and al-Aʿrāf negate any guide; من makes generic negation explicit here, while لا plus an accusative noun does so there, a rhetorical variation.
rows.anchor: والآيتان متساويتان في إفادة نفي جنس الهادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting له before هاد emphasizes their condition: they trust powerless idols to harm the Prophet despite their evident impotence and ignore the true Lord's power.
rows.anchor: وتقديم { له } على { هاد } للاهتمام بضميرهم في مقام نفي الهادي لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis differs from al-Aʿrāf, where misguidance is failure to consider the heavens and earth, less egregious than fearing idols; the following verse assures that the guided remain firm.
rows.anchor: بخلاف آية الأعراف فإن فيها ذكر إعراضهم عن النظر في ملكوت السماوات والأرض وهو ضلال دون ضلال التخويف من بأس أصنامهم

words: ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior contrast presents believers relying on the powerful God and idolaters on impotent idols; God's guidance for the former is firm, so the latter cannot draw them into error.
rows.anchor: فلما بين أن ضلال الفريق الثاني ضلال مكين ببيان أن هدى الفريق الآخر راسخ متين فلا مطمع للفريق الضال بأن يجروا المهتدين إلى ضلالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سيئات is feminine because it commonly describes deeds; although their acquisitions include corrupt beliefs, rancor, grudges, and envy, the familiar feminine usage for acts such as theft, murder, and sexual sins predominates.
rows.anchor: جمع سيئة ، وهو وصف أضيف إلى موصوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says they acquired rather than did these deeds to mark them as the cause of their punishment and end their protest, as in 39:24.
rows.anchor: لقطع تبرمهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحوق means to surround completely so that the surrounded people cannot escape; Ibn Ashur had discussed its etymology at al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: والحوق : الإحاطة ، أي أحاط بهم فلم ينفلتوا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they mocked is the afterlife punishment: the punishment is personified as something mocked; alternatively, the object is omitted and the Prophet is mocked because he mentioned punishment.
rows.anchor: تنزيلا للعقاب منزلة مستهزء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting به highlights the punishment and maintains the verse's cadence.
rows.anchor: للاهتمام به وللرعاية على الفاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء branches from the reaction to hearing God's name alone in 39:45, with intervening linked asides; the striking contrast is that they shun God's name yet call Him alone in distress.
rows.anchor: الفاء لتفريع هذا الكلام على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a sequence of reported episodes rather than worldly causation; unlike the similar opening in 39:8, it begins with فاء. The main consequence is the distress prayer; what follows elaborates it.
rows.anchor: وهذه النكتة هي الفارقة بين العطف بالفاء هنا وعطف نظيرها بالواو في قوله أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in 39:8, الإنسان means the class of polytheists, a generic definite with customary collective scope; the variation makes the repeated passage add something new.
rows.anchor: وأن المراد بالإنسان كل مشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما combines إن with the particle that neutralizes it, yielding restriction like ما...إلا: he claims he received the blessing only through his own knowledge of how to acquire it.
rows.anchor: إنما } فيه هي الكلمة المركبة من ( إن ) الكافة التي تصير كلمة تدل على الحصر بمنزلة ( ما ) النافية التي بعدها ( إلا ) الاستثنائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in أوتيته returns to نعمة, treated as something present before the speaker, so the pronoun functions like a demonstrative; Ibn Ashur compares 46:24.
rows.anchor: وتركيز ضمير الغائب في قوله : { أوتيته } عائد إلى { نعمة } على تأويل حكاية مقالتهم بأنها صادرة منهم في حال حضور ما بين أيديهم من أنواع النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement expresses what they actually believe, since speech follows belief; على gives the cause, meaning that the blessing came because of their knowledge.
rows.anchor: اعتقد ذلك فجرى في أقواله إذ القول على وفق الاعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here knowledge means ordinary acumen and planning, common to practical people; in the Qarun passage it means his special knowledge of gold and silver craft and alchemy that built his wealth.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد بالعلم هنا مجرد الفطنة والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed knowledge is skill at earning and warding off harm, like a sailor's maneuvering in a dangerous sea; the boast answers believers who attribute the blessing to God's favor.
rows.anchor: والمراد : العلم بطرق الكسب ودفع الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل cancels their claim: God gives blessings to reveal how grateful people are, making the blessing a trial of their knowledge of Him and gratitude, though God needs no test to know them.
rows.anchor: وضمير { هي } عائد إلى القول المستفاد من { قال } على طريقة إعادة الضمير على المصدر المأخوذ من فعل نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هي may refer to the statement inferred from قال, to the word understood as a sentence, or to the blessing; the statement can cause a trial or arise from one.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير عائدا إلى نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people, including the speakers, do not realize that worldly blessings can test their response, with ingratitude potentially leading to disbelief.
rows.anchor: لكن لا يعلم أكثر الناس ومنهم القائلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that predecessors said this clarifies that the blessing was a trial: their outcome showed what followed from the boast in 39:49.
rows.anchor: جملة { قد قالها } مبينة لمضمون { هي فتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in قالها refers to the earlier claim إنما أوتيته على علم, construed as a word or sentence; compare the phrase in al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: على تأويل القول بالكلمة التي هي الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predecessors were irreligious people of earlier generations known to God, including Qarun, whom al-Qaṣaṣ says made the same boast.
rows.anchor: ومنهم قارون وقد حكى عنه في سورة القصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their acquisitions were their wealth, which could not protect them from punishment.
rows.anchor: ما كسبوه من أموال

words: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء links the failure of their wealth to their boast; the failure implies grave harm they would seek to ransom, but could not, as the next clause explains.
rows.anchor: فإن عدم الإغناء مشعر بأنهم حل بهم من السوء ما شأن مثله أن يتطلب صاحبه الافتداء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next فاء makes punishment follow the failure of wealth; the normal order would put punishment first, but the reversal quickly refutes the boast that knowledge earned their blessings.
rows.anchor: فعكس الترتيب على خلاف مقتضى الظاهر لقصد التعجيل بإبطال مقالة قائلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هؤلاء refers to Meccan polytheists, usually Quraysh in Ibn Ashur's account of the Qur'an's usage of this demonstrative.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بهؤلاء } إلى المشركين من أهل مكة وقد بينا غير مرة أننا اهتدينا إلى كشف عادة من عادات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil deeds that struck them mean the punishment for evil deeds, in this world and the next; a sin's recompense is a like evil.
rows.anchor: وإصابة السيئات مراد بها في الموضعين إصابة جزاء السيئات وهو عقاب الدنيا وعقاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: معجز means overpowering or escaping God's reach; the object is omitted because context supplies it, as at al-Anʿām 6:134.
rows.anchor: والمعجز : الغالب ، وتقدم

words: أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation rebukes their failure to seek evidence and listen to reminders; they should know God grants or withholds provision as He wills.
rows.anchor: وكان الشأن أن يعلموا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawfiyah is giving something fully, without deficiency from what is due or from what comparable recipients receive.
rows.anchor: والتوفية : إعطاء الشيء وافيا لا نقص فيه عن الحق في إعطائه ولا عن عطاء أمثاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An annexed noun is omitted after ما عملت: the verse means the recompense for what each person did, since the deed itself is not handed back to its doer.
rows.anchor: مضاف محذوف ، أي جزاء ما عملت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense verbs describe future events as certain, as Ibn Ashur explained for the blowing of the Trumpet in 39:68.
rows.anchor: والقول في الأفعال الماضوية في قوله : { وأشرقت } ، { ووضع } ، { وجاء } ، { ووفيت } كالقول في قوله : { ونفخ في الصور }

words: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This carries out the judgment and full recompense announced in 39:69–70: wrongdoers enter punishment and the righteous enter the abode of reward.
rows.anchor: هذا تنفيذ القضاء الذي جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account begins with those due punishment because it renews warning for people unmoved by repeated Qur'anic admonitions; the saved have already responded, so their mention is repeated good news and praise.
rows.anchor: وابتدىء في الخبر بذكر مستحقي العقاب لأنه الأهم في هذا المقام إذ هو مقام إعادة الموعظة والترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Driving means making one walk while another goes ahead and stays beside him; unlike leading, it conveys coercion and humiliation, as in the description of people driven toward death.
rows.anchor: والسوق : أن يجعل الماشي ماشيا آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A zumrah is a group followed by another group; the term implies succession rather than an isolated passing group.
rows.anchor: والزمر : جمع زمرة ، وهي الفوج من الناس المتبوع بفوج آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Groups reflect different degrees of disbelief: if the threat targets Quraysh, their severity, attitude toward Muslims, and treatment of the Prophet distinguish them; if all polytheists, their kinds of shirk distinguish them.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد بهم جميع أهل الشرك كما تقتضيه حكاية الموقف مع قوله : { ألم يأتكم رسل } كان تعدد زمرهم على حسب أنواع إشراكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى begins a new sentence, while إذا is a future time adverb usually carrying a conditional sense; the forceful driving continues until arrival at Hell.
rows.anchor: و { حتى } ابتدائية و { إذا } ظرف لزمان المستقبل يضمن معنى الشرط غالبا

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary point appears in this segment.

words: وما كيد الكافرين إلا في ضلال
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plan was called a plot because they secretly conferred without Moses or his followers knowing; calamities later occupied them and prevented its execution.
rows.anchor: وسمي هذا الرأي كيدا لأنهم تشاوروا فيه فيما بينهم دون أن يعلم بذلك موسى والذين آمنوا معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ضلال means loss and dissipation; God blocked the plot so they found no way to carry it out, as in the image of being lost in the earth.
rows.anchor: والضلال : الضياع والاضمحلال كقوله : { قالوا أئذا ضللنا في الأرض إنا لفي خلق جديد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw marks a separate occasion, not a reply to the proposal to kill the believers' sons; Pharaoh neither endorsed nor rejected it, later choosing to kill Moses alone as a surer way to end their movement.
rows.anchor: عطف { وقال } بالواو يدل على أنه قال هذا القول في موطن آخر ولم يكن جوابا لقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذروني performs a display of desire and awaited approval, as if others restrained Pharaoh; the idiom also implies that the act is dangerous and difficult enough for advisers to discourage.
rows.anchor: ومعنى : { ذروني } إعلامهم بعزمه بضرب من إظهار ميله لذلك وانتظاره الموافقة عليه

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: Ṭarafa's line uses دعني for asking to be left to act when another might restrain the speaker; دعني is the word illustrating this usage.
rows.anchor: قال طرفة : فان كنت لا تستطيع دفع منيتي فدعني أبادرها بما ملكت يدي

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم السهيلي
rows.claim: The idiom دعني and its equivalent خلني commonly express desire even without an actual opponent, as illustrated by al-Suhayli's poem.
rows.anchor: وقول أبي القاسم السهيلي : دعني على حكم الهوى أتضرع فعسى يلين لي الحبيب ويخشع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command lām in وليدع is used to signal indifference: let Moses call on his Lord, as though that made no difference.
rows.anchor: ولام الأمر في { وليدع ربه } مستعملة في التسوية وعدم الاكتراث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fear explains Pharaoh's resolve to kill Moses; خوف means strong apprehension or belief that Moses will change their religion.
rows.anchor: والخوف مستعمل في الإشفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition من normally required by أخاف is omitted because the verb precedes أن.
rows.anchor: وحذفت ( من ) التي يتعدى بها فعل { أخاف } لأنها وقعت بينه وبين ( أن )
